# 0009 — "How this site is built": a page generated by the pipeline

**Date:** 2026-11-04 · **Status:** Accepted

## Context
The site claims tests, quality gates and recorded decisions. The repository proves it to people
who open it; most visitors won't. We wanted the proof on the site itself, without numbers
anyone has to remember to update.

## Decision
- `scripts/metrics.mjs` collects real values and writes `.build-metrics.json` (not committed):
  unit test results (Vitest JSON reporter), the number of end-to-end and accessibility tests
  (`playwright test --list`), ADR titles, workflows, dependency counts, installed versions,
  lines of code and the commit.
- On deploy, Lighthouse runs against the build that is about to be published (collect +
  filesystem upload), the metrics are collected again with those results, and the site is
  rebuilt. The page shows per-URL scores, transfer size and LCP from that run.
- `/pt/build/` and `/en/build/` read the file at build time. Anything not measured shows "—"
  ("measured on deploy") instead of a guess.

## Consequences
- Every deploy builds twice and runs Lighthouse (~3 extra minutes).
- The numbers can go down; the page shows it. CI blocks the PRs that would make them fall below
  the minimums (ADR-0006).
- E2E checks that the page renders real numbers (all unit tests passing, e2e count, 4 workflows,
  every ADR, the commit link).
